_note: Translator glossary. Read this BEFORE translating any pack. Most of these are ordinary English words carrying a domain meaning, so a confident wrong reading produces a translation that looks fine and is wrong. `means` is what Stone Author means. `notThe` is the reading to avoid — usually the first one a dictionary gives. `ruling` is keep (leave the English term), translate, or trade (use your language's established stone/glass/masonry term, and if it genuinely has none, keep the English rather than coin one — a mason searching for an invented word finds nothing).

gauge.means: the thickness of a drawn vein across its width
gauge.notThe: a measuring instrument, a pressure gauge, or a railway gauge
gauge.hint: the sense is line weight / stroke thickness

family.means: a named set of stone characters (Carrara, Calacatta, Nero Marquina, Granite) that decides how veins rough, swell and branch
family.hint: closer to 'type' or 'variety' of stone than to kinship

ground.means: the base surface of the slab, under everything else
ground.notThe: electrical earth, or the floor, or coffee grounds
ground.hint: the painter's sense: the surface you work on top of

matrix.means: the fine-grained rock surrounding the angular fragments in a breccia
matrix.notThe: a mathematical array or a grid
matrix.hint: geological sense; many languages keep a cognate of matrix/matrice here

island.means: a disc-shaped region the warp is not allowed to touch, so it stays undistorted
island.notThe: a landmass in water, or a kitchen island
island.hint: the metaphor is deliberate and worth keeping if your language supports it

warp.means: a field that distorts the whole slab's geometry
warp.notThe: the lengthwise threads in weaving, or faster-than-light travel

moon.means: a tool that warps the geometry as if a gravitational body had passed through it — you drag the body across the slab and the stone deforms in its wake
moon.notThe: a month, a lunar phase, or anything to do with lunar imagery
moon.hint: use your language's ordinary word for the celestial moon. The name is not decorative: the tool models a mass with gravity, so the astronomical word is the correct one. Do NOT rename it after what it does (a 'drag tool' or 'smudge tool') — that loses the model

web.means: a network of fine cracks spreading from a line
web.notThe: the World Wide Web or a web page
web.hint: the sense is a spider's web / a craquelure network

identity.means: a debug view that paints every line in its own colour so each can be told apart
identity.hint: the sense is 'which line is which'

pour.means: a tool that pours material onto the slab in a flowing stream

chip.means: to knock a small corner off a tile edge
chip.notThe: a silicon chip, or a potato chip

seam.means: a thin line or layer of a different material running through the stone

angle.means: a view that colours each speck by the direction it points
angle.notThe: a point of view or an opinion

fold.means: geological folding — how much a vein buckles back on itself
fold.notThe: folding paper, or folding in cooking

spectrum.means: a light value from -1 to 1 that decides which authored emission glows; 0 is daylight
spectrum.notThe: a political spectrum or a broad range

bucket.means: one of five export groupings a layer files into
bucket.notThe: a pail, or a paint-bucket fill tool

light.means: both the illumination of the slab and the Light tool that aims it

slab.means: a cut panel of stone, here 8x5 ft
slab.hint: the stone trade's word for a cut panel: lastra (IT), dalle/tranche (FR), Platte (DE)

vein.means: a mineral-filled fracture running through the stone

stylolite.means: a serrated, toothed seam formed where rock dissolved under pressure
stylolite.hint: an international geological term with direct cognates: stylolithe (FR), Stylolith (DE), stilolite (IT), estilolito (ES)

boudinage.means: a layer stretched until it breaks into sausage-shaped segments
boudinage.hint: already French and used untranslated in geology worldwide

en-echelon.means: parallel segments each offset from the last, like a row of steps
en-echelon.hint: already French and used untranslated in structural geology

breccia.means: rock made of angular fragments cemented together
breccia.hint: already Italian; most languages use a cognate (brèche FR, Brekzie DE, brecha ES)

clast.means: one angular fragment inside a breccia

drusy.means: a surface lined with a crust of tiny sparkling crystals
drusy.hint: Druse (DE), druse/geode (FR/IT); if your language has no adjective, describe the crystal crust

dendritic.means: branching repeatedly like a tree or a frost pattern

halo.means: a wide soft shoulder of colour around a vein

speck.means: one small mineral grain in granite
speck.hint: the sense is a fleck or grain, not a dot of dirt

kerf.means: the width of material a saw blade removes when cutting
kerf.hint: a real trade term, not general English: Schnittfuge/Schnittbreite (DE), trait de scie (FR), spessore di taglio (IT). Do NOT translate it as 'cut' — the width is the point

grout.means: the filler in the gap between laid tiles

subsurface.means: light entering the stone, scattering inside it, and coming back out — what makes marble look lit from within
subsurface.hint: the rendering term (subsurface scattering); many languages keep the English in technical contexts

specular.means: mirror-like reflection; here, how polished the surface reads

fresnel.means: a lens whose surface is cut into concentric stepped rings
fresnel.hint: named after Augustin-Jean Fresnel — a proper noun, never translated

reeded.means: glass moulded into parallel rounded vertical ridges

herringbone.means: a tile pattern of rectangles laid in interlocking Vs
herringbone.hint: a named pattern with an established name in most languages: spina di pesce (IT), point de Hongrie/chevron (FR), Fischgrät (DE)

basketweave.means: a tile pattern of pairs laid alternately across and along

cairo.means: a tiling of identical irregular pentagons, named after Cairo
cairo.hint: a proper noun in the name of the tiling

subway.means: a tile pattern of offset rectangles, named after New York subway tiling
subway.hint: metro (FR/IT/ES) reads better than a literal 'subway' in most languages
